import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a figure with subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
sensor_order = df.groupby('sensor_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', order=sensor_order, ax=ax1, palette='Set2')
ax1.set_title('Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price scatter with sensor type
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
for sensor in df['sensor_type'].unique():
    sensor_data = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax2.scatter(sensor_data['megapixels'], sensor_data['price_usd'], 
               label=sensor, alpha=0.6, s=30)
ax2.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Megapixels vs Price', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper left')
ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 3. Camera count by brand (top 10)
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
brand_counts = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10)
colors = sns.color_palette('viridis', len(brand_counts))
brand_counts.plot(kind='barh', ax=ax3, color=colors)
ax3.set_title('Top 10 Camera Brands by Count', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Number of Models', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax3.invert_yaxis()

# 4. 4K video capability distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
video_4k_counts = df['has_video_4k'].value_counts()
labels = ['No 4K', '4K']
colors_pie = ['#ff9999', '#66b3ff']
ax4.pie(video_4k_counts.values, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
        colors=colors_pie, startangle=90)
ax4.set_title('4K Video Capability', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

# 5. Average price by model year
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, :2])
yearly_price = df.groupby('model_year')['price_usd'].agg(['mean', 'std'])
ax5.plot(yearly_price.index, yearly_price['mean'], marker='o', linewidth=2, 
         color='steelblue', label='Mean Price')
ax5.fill_between(yearly_price.index, 
                  yearly_price['mean'] - yearly_price['std'],
                  yearly_price['mean'] + yearly_price['std'],
                  alpha=0.3, color='steelblue')
ax5.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax5.set_ylabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax5.set_title('Camera Price Trends Over Years', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax5.legend(fontsize=10)
ax5.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 6. Body type distribution
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
body_type_counts = df['body_type'].value_counts()
colors_body = sns.color_palette('Set3', len(body_type_counts))
ax6.bar(range(len(body_type_counts)), body_type_counts.values, color=colors_body)
ax6.set_xticks(range(len(body_type_counts)))
ax6.set_xticklabels(body_type_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=9)
ax6.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=11)
ax6.set_title('Camera Body Types', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax6.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# Main title
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis Dashboard', 
             fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
